thread:
Sam: Quick follow-up to yesterday's postmortem. I proposed a small SLO update and a set of action owners. Wanted to align here.
Jules: saw it, what's the core change?
Sam: keep availability SLA at 99.95 but add a per-cluster throughput soft-SLO for heavy-gen models at 240 rps. Also temporarily relax p99 latency for non-prod gen cohorts from 700ms -> 925ms while batching rollout is staged.
Ravi: ok but we should not silence p99 alerts. propose change to alert severity instead of removing paging.
Tess: agreed. lower severity for a 15% p99 uplift, still page on sustained 25% uplift over 30m.
Sam: proposed alert snippet:
```
ALERT SLO_P99_Uplift
IF (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, job))) > (baseline_p99 * 1.15)
FOR 30m
LABELS {severity="critical"}
ANNOTATIONS { runbook="/runbooks/slo-p99" }
```
Jules: small wording change: use job="model-runtime" and include model_tag label.
Sam: noted. ownership plan: 1) dashboard panel for recurring-patterns by model_tag and client_tier (owner: Jules, due: 2123458800) 2) implement per-cluster throughput SLO and routing rule (owner: Ravi, due: 2123462400) 3) add adjusted alerting + runbook links (owner: Tess, due: 2123457600) 4) regression weekly job (owner: Sam, due: 2123466000).
Ravi: I'll add a test harness to simulate heavy-gen flows and validate routing.
Tess: I'll update the SLO doc and add the rotation calendar. Also will coordinate with support on customer-facing thresholds.
ops-bot: Incident #4850 updated: root cause = worker pool saturation; mitigation = throttled background jobs, extended KV TTL.
Jules: question: do we notify customers about temporary SLO delta?
Sam: not by default. only if customer impact > 1% of requests or persistent for >24h.
Ravi: logging follow-up ticket to capture customer thresholds and comms plan.
Tess: I'll run the first regression check next Monday and post results.
Sam: thanks all. check-in Wednesday 09:00 to review dashboard + tests. :thumbsup:
